title: 2.13 seconds (Hikaru sees Magnus losing, Baku 2023) x Chessnut Move
post: Hikaru needed 2.13 seconds. How long did you need? ⏱️ #ad #chessnut #chess #hikaru #magnuscarlsen #story

voice._name: Callum (ElevenLabs premade), eleven_v3 with audio tags in "say"

phrases.text: Keymer had thirty seconds. Magnus had thirty-two minutes.
phrases.say: [tense] Keymer had thirty seconds. Magnus had... thirty-two minutes.

phrases.text: Hikaru walked by, and the internet timed it: 2.13 seconds to see Magnus was losing.
phrases.say: Hikaru walked by... and the internet timed it. [dramatic] Two point one three seconds... to see Magnus was losing.

phrases.text: What did he see? A knight hitting two pawns at once. One fell, and twenty moves later, Magnus resigned.
phrases.say: [curious] What did he see? A knight hitting two pawns at once. One fell... and twenty moves later, Magnus resigned.

phrases.text: And that's not even the scary part.
phrases.say: [dramatic] And that's not even the scary part.

phrases.text: Blindfold against Magnus, a pawn down, he saw a bishop sacrifice that forced a draw.
phrases.say: Blindfold against Magnus... a pawn down... he saw a bishop sacrifice that forced a draw.

phrases.text: This October, he became the first ever to hit 3500 in blitz on Chess.com.
phrases.say: [excited] This October, he became the first ever to hit thirty-five hundred... in blitz, on Chess dot com.

phrases.text: On the way: 34 straight wins in one day. Magnus? A hundred points behind.
phrases.say: On the way... thirty-four straight wins in one day. Magnus? A hundred points behind.

phrases.text: He doesn't need Stockfish. He IS the engine.
phrases.say: He doesn't need Stockfish... [dramatic] he IS the engine.

phrases.text: So how did he know? Show a grandmaster a real position for five seconds, and he rebuilds it.
phrases.say: So how did he know? Show a grandmaster a real position for five seconds... and he rebuilds it.

phrases.text: Scramble the pieces, and he's barely better than a beginner.
phrases.say: Scramble the pieces... and he's barely better than a beginner.

phrases.text: He sees patterns, not pieces. About fifty thousand.
phrases.say: [impressed] He sees patterns, not pieces. About fifty thousand.

phrases.text: That's skill one. Skill two: a board in his head, where pieces play out whole combinations on their own.
phrases.say: That's skill one. Skill two... a board in his head, where pieces play out whole combinations on their own.

phrases.text: Pieces that move on their own? That's the Chessnut Move.
phrases.say: Pieces that move on their own? That's the Chessnut Move.

phrases.text: Each piece has its own motor. Snap a photo of any position, and it sets itself up.
phrases.say: Each piece has its own motor. Snap a photo of any position... and it sets itself up.

phrases.text: Play Chess.com or Lichess on a real board. After the game, all 32 pieces drive home.
phrases.say: Play Chess dot com or Lichess on a real board. After the game... all thirty-two pieces drive home.

phrases.text: Hikaru needed two seconds. How many did you need?
phrases.say: [curious] Hikaru needed two seconds... How many did you need?
